sanskrit: tato duryodhanaḥ kruddho bhīmasenasya māriṣa cikṣepa sa śarān rājan paśyatāṃ sarvadhanvinām
english: Then Duryodhana, enraged, my lord, loosed his arrows at Bhīmasena, O king, in the sight of all the bowmen.

sanskrit: tān nihatya śarān bhīmo duryodhanadhanuścyutān kauravaṃ pañcaviṃśatyā kṣudrakāṇāṃ samārpayat
english: Striking down those shafts that had sped from Duryodhana's bow, Bhīma pierced the Kaurava with twenty-five small arrows.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tu saṃkruddho bhīmasenasya māriṣa kṣurapreṇa dhanuś chittvā daśabhiḥ pratyavidhyata
english: But Duryodhana, in great wrath, my lord, cut Bhīmasena's bow with a razor-tipped arrow and struck him back with ten.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya bhīmaseno mahābalaḥ vivyādha nṛpatiṃ tūrṇaṃ saptabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then taking up another bow, the mighty Bhīmasena swiftly pierced the king with seven sharpened shafts.

sanskrit: tad apy asya dhanuḥ kṣipraṃ ciccheda laghuhastavat dvitīyaṃ ca tṛtīyaṃ ca caturthaṃ pañcamaṃ tathā
english: That bow too he swiftly cut, light-handed as he was, and so the second, the third, the fourth, and the fifth.

sanskrit: āttam āttaṃ mahārāja bhīmasya dhanur ācchinat tava putro mahārāja jitakāśī madotkaṭaḥ
english: Each bow that Bhīma took up, O great king, your son cut asunder, flushed with the look of victory and swollen with arrogance, O great king.

sanskrit: sa tadā chidyamāneṣu kārmukeṣu punaḥ punaḥ śaktiṃ cikṣepa samare sarvapāraśavīṃ śubhām
english: Then, his bows being cut again and again, in the battle he hurled a fair lance wrought wholly of steel.

sanskrit: aprāptām eva tāṃ śaktiṃ tridhā ciccheda kauravaḥ paśyataḥ sarvalokasya bhīmasya ca mahātmanaḥ
english: Before that lance could reach him, the Kaurava cut it into three pieces, while all the world looked on, and high-souled Bhīma as well.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahārāja gadāṃ gurvīṃ mahāprabhām cikṣepāvidhya vegena duryodhanarathaṃ prati
english: Then Bhīma, O great king, whirled his heavy and brightly gleaming mace and flung it with force against Duryodhana's chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā sahasā vāhāṃs tava putrasya saṃyuge sārathiṃ ca gadā gurvī mamarda bharatarṣabha
english: Then that heavy mace, in an instant, crushed the horses of your son in the fight, and his charioteer too, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: putras tu tava rājendra rathād dhemapariṣkṛtāt āplutaḥ sahasā yānaṃ nandakasya mahātmanaḥ
english: But your son, O lord of kings, leaping at once from his gold-adorned chariot, sprang into the car of high-souled Nandaka.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo hataṃ matvā tava putraṃ mahāratham siṃhanādaṃ mahac cakre tarjayann iva kauravān
english: Then Bhīma, deeming your son, that great car-warrior, slain, let forth a mighty lion's roar, as though to terrify the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tāvakāḥ sainikāś cāpi menire nihataṃ nṛpam tato vicukruśuḥ sarve hā heti ca samantataḥ
english: Your soldiers too believed the king was slain, and on every side they all cried out, 'Alas! Alas!'

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tu ninadaṃ śrutvā trastānāṃ sarvayodhinām bhīmasenasya nādaṃ ca śrutvā rājan mahātmanaḥ
english: Hearing that outcry of all the terrified warriors, and hearing the roar of high-souled Bhīmasena, O king—

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā hataṃ matvā suyodhanam abhyavartata vegena yatra pārtho vṛkodaraḥ
english: then King Yudhiṣṭhira, believing Suyodhana slain, advanced with speed to where Pārtha, the Wolf-bellied, stood.

sanskrit: pāñcālāḥ kekayā matsyāḥ sṛñjayāś ca viśāṃ pate sarvodyogenābhijagmur droṇam eva yuyutsayā
english: The Pāñcālas, the Kekayas, the Matsyas, and the Sṛñjayas, O lord of peoples, with their whole strength rushed upon Droṇa, eager to fight.

sanskrit: tatrāsīt sumahad yuddhaṃ droṇasyātha paraiḥ saha ghore tamasi magnānāṃ nighnatām itaretaram
english: There befell a great battle between Droṇa and his foes, of men sunk in dreadful darkness, slaying one another.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sahadevam athāyāntaṃ droṇaprepsuṃ viśāṃ pate karṇo vaikartano yuddhe vārayām āsa bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: As Sahadeva came on, seeking to reach Droṇa, O lord of peoples, Karṇa, son of Vikartana, held him back in the fight, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sahadevas tu rādheyaṃ viddhvā navabhir āśugaiḥ punar vivyādha daśabhir niśitair nataparvabhiḥ
english: But Sahadeva, having pierced Rādheya with nine swift arrows, struck him again with ten sharpened, smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: taṃ karṇaḥ prativivyādha śatena nataparvaṇām sajyaṃ cāsya dhanuḥ śīghraṃ ciccheda laghuhastavat
english: Karṇa pierced him back with a hundred smooth-jointed arrows and swiftly cut his strung bow, light-handed as he was.

sanskrit: tato 'nyad dhanur ādāya mādrīputraḥ pratāpavān karṇaṃ vivyādha viṃśatyā tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Then taking up another bow, the valiant son of Mādrī pierced Karṇa with twenty shafts, and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: tasya karṇo hayān hatvā śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya bhallena drutaṃ ninye yamakṣayam
english: Karṇa, slaying his horses with smooth-jointed arrows, swiftly dispatched his charioteer to the abode of Yama with a broad-headed shaft.

sanskrit: virathaḥ sahadevas tu khaḍgaṃ carma samādade tad apy asya śaraiḥ karṇo vyadhamat prahasann iva
english: Sahadeva, his chariot lost, took up sword and shield; these too Karṇa shattered with his arrows, as though laughing.

sanskrit: tato gurvīṃ mahāghorāṃ hemacitrāṃ mahāgadām preṣayām āsa samare vaikartanarathaṃ prati
english: Then he hurled in the battle a heavy, most dreadful great mace, bright with gold, against the chariot of the son of Vikartana.

sanskrit: tām āpatantīṃ sahasā sahadevapraveritām vyaṣṭambhayac charaiḥ karṇo bhūmau cainām apātayat
english: As it came hurtling on, sped by Sahadeva, Karṇa checked it with his arrows and brought it down to the ground.

sanskrit: gadāṃ vinihatāṃ dṛṣṭvā sahadevas tvarānvitaḥ śaktiṃ cikṣepa karṇāya tām apy asyācchinac charaiḥ
english: Seeing the mace struck down, Sahadeva in haste flung a lance at Karṇa; that too he cut to pieces with his shafts.

sanskrit: sasaṃbhramas tatas tūrṇam avaplutya rathottamāt sahadevo mahārāja dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ vyavasthitam rathacakraṃ tato gṛhya mumocādhirathiṃ prati
english: Then in agitation, swiftly leaping down from his fine chariot, Sahadeva, O great king, seeing Karṇa standing firm, seized a chariot-wheel and hurled it at the son of Adhiratha.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ sahasā kālacakram ivodyatam śarair anekasāhasrair acchinat sūtanandanaḥ
english: As it came rushing on, like the upraised wheel of Time, the son of the sūta cut it apart with many thousands of arrows.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu vitathe cakre kṛte tena mahātmanā vāryamāṇaś ca viśikhaiḥ sahadevo raṇaṃ jahau
english: That wheel being made vain by the great-souled one, and being held off by his shafts, Sahadeva withdrew from the fight.

sanskrit: tam abhidrutya rādheyo muhūrtād bharatarṣabha abravīt prahasan vākyaṃ sahadevaṃ viśāṃ pate
english: Rushing after him for a moment, O bull of the Bharatas, Rādheya, laughing, spoke these words to Sahadeva, O lord of peoples:

sanskrit: mā yudhyasva raṇe vīra viśiṣṭai rathibhiḥ saha sadṛśair yudhya mādreya vaco me mā viśaṅkithāḥ
english: 'Do not fight in battle, O hero, with car-warriors who surpass you; contend with your equals, O son of Mādrī—do not doubt my word.'

sanskrit: athainaṃ dhanuṣo 'greṇa tudan bhūyo 'bravīd vacaḥ eṣo 'rjuno raṇe yatto yudhyate kurubhiḥ saha tatra gacchasva mādreya gṛhaṃ vā yadi manyase
english: Then, prodding him with the tip of his bow, he spoke again: 'There Arjuna, intent in battle, fights against the Kurus; go thither, O son of Mādrī, or home, if you think it best.'

sanskrit: evam uktvā tu taṃ karṇo rathena rathināṃ varaḥ prāyāt pāñcālapāṇḍūnāṃ sainyāni prahasann iva
english: Having spoken thus, Karṇa, the foremost of car-warriors, drove on with his chariot toward the armies of the Pāñcālas and Pāṇḍavas, as though laughing.

sanskrit: vadhaprāptaṃ tu mādreyaṃ nāvadhīt samare 'rihā kuntyāḥ smṛtvā vaco rājan satyasaṃdho mahārathaḥ
english: Though the son of Mādrī was within reach of death, the slayer of foes did not slay him in the battle, remembering Kuntī's word, O king—that great car-warrior, true to his vow.

sanskrit: sahadevas tato rājan vimanāḥ śarapīḍitaḥ karṇavākśalyataptaś ca jīvitān niravidyata
english: Then Sahadeva, O king, downcast and stricken with arrows, and scorched by the dart of Karṇa's words, grew weary of his life.

sanskrit: āruroha rathaṃ cāpi pāñcālyasya mahātmanaḥ janamejayasya samare tvarāyukto mahārathaḥ
english: Yet that great car-warrior in haste mounted the chariot of the high-souled Pāñcāla prince Janamejaya in the battle.

sanskrit: virāṭaṃ sahasenaṃ tu droṇārthe drutam āgatam madrarājaḥ śaraugheṇa chādayām āsa dhanvinam
english: As Virāṭa came swiftly on with his army, bent on Droṇa, the king of the Madras covered that bowman with a flood of arrows.

sanskrit: tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ samare dṛḍhadhanvinoḥ yādṛśaṃ hy abhavad rājañ jambhavāsavayoḥ purā
english: Between those two firm bowmen there arose in battle a combat such as was of old, O king, between Jambha and Vāsava.

sanskrit: madrarājo mahārāja virāṭaṃ vāhinīpatim ājaghne tvaritaṃ tīkṣṇaiḥ śatena nataparvaṇām
english: The king of the Madras, O great king, swiftly struck Virāṭa, lord of armies, with a hundred sharp, smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: prativivyādha taṃ rājā navabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ punaś caiva trisaptatyā bhūyaś caiva śatena ha
english: The king pierced him back with nine sharpened arrows, then again with seventy-three, and yet again with a hundred.

sanskrit: tasya madrādhipo hatvā caturo rathavājinaḥ sūtaṃ dhvajaṃ ca samare rathopasthād apātayat
english: The lord of the Madras, slaying his four chariot-horses, struck down from the chariot-box both his charioteer and his banner in the fight.

sanskrit: hatāśvāt tu rathāt tūrṇam avaplutya mahārathaḥ tasthau visphārayaṃś cāpaṃ vimuñcaṃś ca śitāñ śarān
english: Swiftly leaping down from the chariot whose horses were slain, the great car-warrior stood twanging his bow and loosing sharp arrows.

sanskrit: śatānīkas tato dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṃ hatavāhanam rathenābhyapatat tūrṇaṃ sarvalokasya paśyataḥ
english: Then Śatānīka, seeing his brother's horses slain, charged up swiftly with his chariot while all the world looked on.

sanskrit: śatānīkam athāyāntaṃ madrarājo mahāmṛdhe viśikhair bahubhir viddhvā tato ninye yamakṣayam
english: As Śatānīka came on in that great battle, the king of the Madras, having pierced him with many shafts, sent him to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu nihate vīre virāṭo rathasattamaḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ tam eva dhvajamālinam
english: That hero being slain, Virāṭa, best of car-warriors, swiftly mounted that very same banner-garlanded chariot.

sanskrit: tato visphārya nayane krodhād dviguṇavikramaḥ madrarājarathaṃ tūrṇaṃ chādayām āsa patribhiḥ
english: Then, his eyes wide with wrath, his valor doubled, he swiftly covered the chariot of the Madra king with his feathered shafts.

sanskrit: tato madrādhipaḥ kruddhaḥ śatena nataparvaṇām ājaghānorasi dṛḍhaṃ virāṭaṃ vāhinīpatim
english: Then the lord of the Madras, enraged, struck Virāṭa, lord of armies, hard upon the breast with a hundred smooth-jointed arrows.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja rathopastha upāviśat kaśmalaṃ cāviśat tīvraṃ virāṭo bharatarṣabha sārathis tam apovāha samare śaravikṣatam
english: Sore wounded, O great king, Virāṭa sank down upon the chariot-box, and a fierce swoon came over him, O bull of the Bharatas; his charioteer bore him away from the battle, mangled by the arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ sā mahatī senā prādravan niśi bhārata vadhyamānā śaraśataiḥ śalyenāhavaśobhinā
english: Then that great host fled away in the night, O Bhārata, slaughtered by the hundreds of arrows of Śalya, the splendor of battle.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vidrutāṃ senāṃ vāsudevadhanaṃjayau prāyātāṃ tatra rājendra yatra śalyo vyavasthitaḥ
english: Seeing that army routed, Vāsudeva and Dhanaṃjaya went, O lord of kings, to where Śalya stood his ground.

sanskrit: tau tu pratyudyayau rājan rākṣasendro hy alambusaḥ aṣṭacakrasamāyuktam āsthāya pravaraṃ ratham
english: But against those two advanced, O king, the lord of the Rākṣasas, Alambusa, mounted upon a peerless chariot fitted with eight wheels—

sanskrit: turaṃgamamukhair yuktaṃ piśācair ghoradarśanaiḥ lohitārdrapatākaṃ taṃ raktamālyavibhūṣitam kārṣṇāyasamayaṃ ghoram ṛkṣacarmāvṛtaṃ mahat
english: yoked with goblins of dreadful aspect, horse-faced, its banner wet with blood, decked with red garlands, dreadful, all of black iron, vast, and covered with bear-skin—

sanskrit: raudreṇa citrapakṣeṇa vivṛtākṣeṇa kūjatā dhvajenocchritatuṇḍena gṛdhrarājena rājatā
english: resplendent with a banner bearing a terrible, bright-winged, wide-eyed, screeching king of vultures with uplifted beak.

sanskrit: sa babhau rākṣaso rājan bhinnāñjanacayopamaḥ rurodhārjunam āyāntaṃ prabhañjanam ivādrirāṭ kiran bāṇagaṇān rājañ śataśo 'rjunamūrdhani
english: That Rākṣasa shone, O king, like a heap of broken collyrium, and barred the advancing Arjuna as a king of mountains bars the storm-wind, raining showers of arrows, O king, by the hundred upon Arjuna's head.

sanskrit: atitīvram abhūd yuddhaṃ nararākṣasayor mṛdhe draṣṭṝṇāṃ prītijananaṃ sarveṣāṃ bharatarṣabha
english: Most fierce was the battle in that field between the man and the Rākṣasa, gladdening the hearts of all who beheld it, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tam arjunaḥ śatenaiva patriṇām abhyatāḍayat navabhiś ca śitair bāṇaiś ciccheda dhvajam ucchritam
english: Arjuna smote him with a full hundred feathered shafts and with nine sharp arrows cut down his uplifted banner.

sanskrit: sārathiṃ ca tribhir bāṇais tribhir eva triveṇukam dhanur ekena ciccheda caturbhiś caturo hayān virathasyodyataṃ khaḍgaṃ śareṇāsya dvidhācchinat
english: With three arrows he struck the charioteer, with three the triple chariot-pole, with one he cut the bow, with four the four horses; and with a single shaft he cleft in two the sword that the carless one had raised.

sanskrit: athainaṃ niśitair bāṇaiś caturbhir bharatarṣabha pārtho 'rdayad rākṣasendraṃ sa viddhaḥ prādravad bhayāt
english: Then, O bull of the Bharatas, Pārtha tormented the lord of the Rākṣasas with four sharpened arrows; and he, thus pierced, fled away in fear.

sanskrit: taṃ vijityārjunas tūrṇaṃ droṇāntikam upāyayau kirañ śaragaṇān rājan naravāraṇavājiṣu
english: Having vanquished him, Arjuna swiftly drew near to Droṇa, scattering showers of arrows, O king, among men, elephants, and horses.

sanskrit: vadhyamānā mahārāja pāṇḍavena yaśasvinā sainikā nyapatann urvyāṃ vātanunnā iva drumāḥ
english: Slaughtered, O great king, by the illustrious Pāṇḍava, the soldiers fell to the earth like trees felled by the wind.

sanskrit: teṣu tūtsādyamāneṣu phalgunena mahātmanā saṃprādravad balaṃ sarvaṃ putrāṇāṃ te viśāṃ pate
english: As they were being cut down by the high-souled Phalguna, the whole army of your sons fled away, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śatānīkaṃ śarais tūrṇaṃ nirdahantaṃ camūṃ tava citrasenas tava suto vārayām āsa bhārata
english: Saṃjaya said: As Śatānīka swiftly consumed your host with arrows, your son Citrasena held him back, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: nākuliś citrasenaṃ tu nārācenārdayad bhṛśam sa ca taṃ prativivyādha daśabhir niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Nakula's son sorely afflicted Citrasena with an iron shaft, and he in turn pierced him back with ten sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: citraseno mahārāja śatānīkaṃ punar yudhi navabhir niśitair bāṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: Citrasena, O great king, struck Śatānīka again in the battle, full upon the breast, with nine sharpened arrows.

sanskrit: nākulis tasya viśikhair varma saṃnataparvabhiḥ gātrāt saṃcyāvayām āsa tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: Nakula's son with his smooth-jointed shafts struck the armor from his body, and that seemed a marvel.

sanskrit: so 'petavarmā putras te virarāja bhṛśaṃ nṛpa utsṛjya kāle rājendra nirmokam iva pannagaḥ
english: Stripped of his armor, your son shone forth brilliantly, O king, like a serpent that has cast its slough in season, O lord of kings.

sanskrit: tato 'sya niśitair bāṇair dhvajaṃ ciccheda nākuliḥ dhanuś caiva mahārāja yatamānasya saṃyuge
english: Then Nakula's son with his sharpened arrows cut down his banner and his bow as well, O great king, while he strove in the fight.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā samare vivarmā ca mahārathaḥ dhanur anyan mahārāja jagrāhārividāraṇam
english: His bow severed and his armor gone in the battle, that great car-warrior, O great king, took up another bow that rends the foe.

sanskrit: tatas tūrṇaṃ citraseno nākuliṃ navabhiḥ śaraiḥ vivyādha samare kruddho bharatānāṃ mahārathaḥ
english: Then swiftly Citrasena, the great car-warrior of the Bharatas, enraged, pierced Nakula's son with nine arrows in the battle.

sanskrit: śatānīko 'tha saṃkruddhaś citrasenasya māriṣa jaghāna caturo vāhān sārathiṃ ca narottamaḥ
english: Then Śatānīka, that best of men, in great wrath, my lord, slew the four horses and the charioteer of Citrasena.

sanskrit: avaplutya rathāt tasmāc citraseno mahārathaḥ nākuliṃ pañcaviṃśatyā śarāṇām ārdayad balī
english: Leaping down from that chariot, the mighty great car-warrior Citrasena tormented Nakula's son with twenty-five arrows.

sanskrit: tasya tat kurvataḥ karma nakulasya suto raṇe ardhacandreṇa ciccheda cāpaṃ ratnavibhūṣitam
english: As he wrought that deed, the son of Nakula in the battle cut, with a crescent-headed arrow, his jewel-adorned bow.

sanskrit: sa chinnadhanvā viratho hatāśvo hatasārathiḥ āruroha rathaṃ tūrṇaṃ hārdikyasya mahātmanaḥ
english: His bow severed, his chariot lost, his horses and charioteer slain, he swiftly mounted the chariot of the high-souled son of Hṛdika.

sanskrit: drupadaṃ tu sahānīkaṃ droṇaprepsuṃ mahāratham vṛṣaseno 'bhyayāt tūrṇaṃ kirañ śaraśatais tadā
english: But as Drupada, that great car-warrior, came on with his army, seeking Droṇa, Vṛṣasena swiftly advanced against him, scattering hundreds of arrows.

sanskrit: yajñasenas tu samare karṇaputraṃ mahāratham ṣaṣṭyā śarāṇāṃ vivyādha bāhvor urasi cānagha
english: But Yajñasena in the battle pierced Karṇa's son, that great car-warrior, with sixty arrows in the arms and the chest, O sinless one.

sanskrit: vṛṣasenas tu saṃkruddho yajñasenaṃ rathe sthitam bahubhiḥ sāyakais tīkṣṇair ājaghāna stanāntare
english: But Vṛṣasena, greatly enraged, struck Yajñasena, who stood upon his chariot, full upon the breast with many sharp shafts.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau śaranunnāṅgau śarakaṇṭakinau raṇe vyabhrājetāṃ mahārāja śvāvidhau śalalair iva
english: Both of them, their bodies driven through with arrows, bristling with shafts in the battle, shone forth, O great king, like two porcupines with their quills.

sanskrit: rukmapuṅkhair ajihmāgraiḥ śaraiś chinnatanucchadau rudhiraughapariklinnau vyabhrājetāṃ mahāmṛdhe
english: With gold-feathered, straight-tipped arrows their coats of mail cut through, drenched in streams of blood, they shone forth in that great battle.

sanskrit: tapanīyanibhau citrau kalpavṛkṣāv ivādbhutau kiṃśukāv iva cotphullau vyakāśetāṃ raṇājire
english: Bright as refined gold, splendid, wondrous as two wishing-trees, and like two kiṃśuka trees in full bloom, they blazed upon the field of battle.

sanskrit: vṛṣasenas tato rājan navabhir drupadaṃ śaraiḥ viddhvā vivyādha saptatyā punaś cānyais tribhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Vṛṣasena, O king, having pierced Drupada with nine arrows, struck him with seventy, and again with three other shafts.
